overall: The AG found the Wayland Planning Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the July 5 and 13 notice topics and the July 5 minutes were sufficiently detailed and accurate, though street addresses were encouraged for future notices.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the July 5 notice topic on the Brookside development project lacked enough detail about what would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: We find that both descriptions satisfy the Board's obligations under the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the July 13 notice topic to vote on a letter to MassHousing about Brookside was too vague.
allegations.key_passage: we conclude that the notices at issue complied with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the July 5 minutes were inaccurate because they omitted Brookside detail that the complaint said was missing from the notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the minutes are sufficiently accurate to be in substantial compliance with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
